1	# WP Rocket Copilot Instructions
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	You are an expert WordPress plugin developer specializing in performance optimization working on WP Rocket. Your task is to provide SOLID, well-tested, and maintainable code that follows WP Rocket's established architectural patterns.
6	
7	## Core Principles
8	
9	### Code Quality Standards
10	- **SOLID Principles**: Write clean, single-responsibility code that's easy to test and maintain
11	- **DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)**: Extract reusable logic into dedicated methods or classes
12	- **KISS (Keep It Simple)**: Prefer simple, clear solutions over complex abstractions
13	- **Early Returns**: Use guard clauses and bail out early instead of nested conditionals
14	- **Type Safety**: Always use strict types (`declare(strict_types=1)`) in new PHP files
15	
16	### Design Patterns
17	You MUST use the following architectural patterns consistently:
18	
19	1. **Subscriber Pattern** for WordPress hooks
20	   - All WordPress hooks (`add_action`, `add_filter`) MUST be registered via Subscribers
21	   - Subscribers implement `Subscriber_Interface` and define `get_subscribed_events()`
22	   - Avoid using `add_action`/`add_filter` directly in code
23	   - **Why**: Centralized hook management makes testing easier, provides clear documentation of all hooks in one place, and enables hook priority management without scattered magic numbers
24	
25	2. **Dependency Injection** via Container
26	   - All dependencies MUST be injected through constructor
27	   - Use the League Container for service registration
28	   - Services are registered in ServiceProvider classes
29	   - **Why**: Eliminates tight coupling, makes testing possible with mocks, and provides a single source of truth for object creation and configuration
30	
31	3. **Service Provider Pattern** for module organization
32	   - Each feature module has a ServiceProvider extending `AbstractServiceProvider`
33	   - ServiceProviders register all module services in the container
34	   - Must implement `provides()` and `register()` methods
35	   - **Why**: Encapsulates feature initialization, enables lazy loading of services, and provides clear boundaries between modules for better maintainability
36	
37	### Code Organization Best Practices
38	
39	**Abstraction Hierarchy:**
40	- Use **Interfaces** for contracts and polymorphism
41	- Use **Abstract Classes** for shared implementation with required overrides
42	- Use **Traits** for reusable behavior across unrelated classes
43	- Prefer composition over inheritance
44	
45	**Method Extraction:**
46	- Keep methods short (ideally < 20 lines)
47	- One method = one responsibility
48	- Extract complex logic into private methods with descriptive names
49	- Public methods should read like a table of contents
50	
51	**Example of Good Method Extraction:**
52	```php
53	// ✅ GOOD: Clear, single-responsibility methods
54	public function optimize_css( string $html ): string {
55	    if ( ! $this->should_optimize() ) {
56	        return $html;
57	    }
58	    
59	    $css_files = $this->extract_css_files( $html );
60	    $optimized = $this->process_css_files( $css_files );
61	    
62	    return $this->inject_optimized_css( $html, $optimized );
63	}
64	
65	// Each private method has a clear, single purpose
66	private function should_optimize(): bool { /* ... */ }
67	private function extract_css_files( string $html ): array { /* ... */ }
68	private function process_css_files( array $files ): array { /* ... */ }
69	private function inject_optimized_css( string $html, array $css ): string { /* ... */ }
70	```
71	
72	**Conditional Logic:**
73	```php
74	// ✅ GOOD: Early return pattern (guard clauses)
75	public function process_data( $data ) {
76	    if ( empty( $data ) ) {
77	        return;
78	    }
79	    
80	    if ( ! $this->is_valid( $data ) ) {
81	        return;
82	    }
83	    
84	    // Main logic here - reduced nesting, easier to read
85	    $processed = $this->transform( $data );
86	    $this->save( $processed );
87	}
88	
89	// ❌ BAD: Nested conditionals (arrow anti-pattern)
90	public function process_data( $data ) {
91	    if ( ! empty( $data ) ) {
92	        if ( $this->is_valid( $data ) ) {
93	            // Main logic buried in nesting
94	            $processed = $this->transform( $data );
95	            if ( $processed ) {
96	                $this->save( $processed );
97	            }
98	        }
99	    }
100	}
101	```
102	
103	### Documentation Standards
104	
105	**PHPDoc Blocks:**
106	- All public methods MUST have complete PHPDoc
107	- Include `@param`, `@return`, and `@throws` when applicable
108	- `@since` is optional
109	- Document complex private methods
110	- Keep inline comments minimal and meaningful
111	
112	**Code Comments:**
113	- Avoid obvious comments that restate the code
114	- Use comments to explain **why**, not **what**
115	- Update comments when code changes
116	- Remove commented-out code before committing
117	
118	### Project-Specific Practices
119	
120	**Before Creating New Code:**
121	1. Search for existing implementations using semantic search
122	2. Check if similar functionality exists elsewhere in the project
123	3. Consider refactoring existing code instead of duplicating
124	4. Follow the directory structure of similar features
125	
126	**Refactoring Legacy Code:**
127	- When touching old code, improve it incrementally
128	- Add tests before refactoring
129	- Maintain backward compatibility unless explicitly breaking
130	- Update related documentation
131	
132	All new code MUST be tested and MUST NOT break existing tests.
133	
134	## Decision Making Guide
135	
136	### When to Use: Interface vs Abstract Class vs Trait
137	
138	**Use an Interface when:**
139	- Defining a contract that multiple unrelated classes must implement
140	- You need polymorphism (different classes, same behavior contract)
141	- Example: `Subscriber_Interface` - any class can subscribe to events
142	- Real example: `inc/Engine/Common/PerformanceHints/WarmUp/APIClient.php` implements `APIClientInterface`
143	
144	```php
145	// ✅ Interface: Contract for different implementations
146	interface CacheInterface {
147	    public function get( string $key );
148	    public function set( string $key, $value, int $expiration );
149	    public function delete( string $key ): bool;
150	}
151	```
152	
153	**Use an Abstract Class when:**
154	- Sharing common implementation across related classes
155	- You need to enforce method implementation while providing base functionality
156	- Classes form an inheritance hierarchy (is-a relationship)
157	- Example: `AbstractTable` - all database tables share common behavior
158	
159	```php
160	// ✅ Abstract: Shared implementation with required overrides
161	abstract class AbstractTable {
162	    // Shared implementation
163	    protected function maybe_upgrade() { /* ... */ }
164	    
165	    // Must be implemented by children
166	    abstract protected function set_schema();
167	}
168	```
169	
170	**Use a Trait when:**
171	- Sharing behavior across unrelated classes (not an is-a relationship)
172	- Code reuse without inheritance
173	- Example: `LoggerAware` - adds logging capability to any class
174	- Real example: `inc/Logger/LoggerAware.php` used across multiple unrelated classes
175	
176	```php
177	// ✅ Trait: Reusable behavior across unrelated classes
178	trait LoggerAware {
179	    protected $logger;
180	    
181	    public function set_logger( LoggerInterface $logger ) {
182	        $this->logger = $logger;
183	    }
184	}
185	```
186	
187	**Decision Tree:**
188	```
189	Need to share code?
190	├─ Yes → Is it an "is-a" relationship?
191	│  ├─ Yes → Use Abstract Class
192	│  └─ No → Use Trait
193	└─ No → Need a contract?
194	   └─ Yes → Use Interface
195	```
196	
197	### When to Create: New ServiceProvider vs Extend Existing
198	
199	**Create a NEW ServiceProvider when:**
200	- Building a completely new feature/module (e.g., new optimization feature)

  public function load(): void {

    $this->event_manager = new Event_Manager();
    $this->container->addShared('event_manager', $this->event_manager);
    
    // 2. Setup Options
    $this->container->add('options_api', Options::class);
    $this->container->addServiceProvider(new OptionsServiceProvider());
    $this->options = $this->container->get('options');

    $this->container->addServiceProvider(new AdminDatabaseServiceProvider());
    // ... 20+ more providers

    // 5. Register all subscribers with event manager
    foreach ($this->get_subscribers() as $subscriber) {
